Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed by the predictable latency and the routing options. Level-set here on what we expect and what we need from Redwood:

Markus / team — quick sizing sketch after looking at the traffic sample:

Summary recommendation (initial commit):
- US pool: 8x H100e (or 12x A100 80GB equivalent) as the reserved baseline. Configure autoscaling to allow +4 nodes burst (on-demand) during reporting windows.
- EU pool: 4x H100e reserved in eu-west region (to satisfy residency). Burst +2 on-demand.
- APAC pilot: 2x H100e in ap-southeast-1 (SG) as reserved, plus hosted fallback for non-critical users.

Rationale:
- Embeddings latency <100ms requires low-latency NVLink topology; H100 provides headroom for peak bursts and batching.
- 18 qps embeddings + 12 qps chat maps to the US baseline above once you account for batching and prefix caching. We modeled token-length distribution from the sample file (attached spreadsheet).

Estimated committed monthly spend (very rough):
- US baseline (8 H100 reserved): ~$320k/month
- EU baseline (4 H100 reserved): ~$160k/month
- APAC pilot (2 H100 reserved): ~$80k/month
- Total committed baseline: ~$560k/month (12-month term)

PoC plan: 2-week PoC (thinly provisioned) -> 2-week performance validation (slo tests & regression checks) -> canary (10% traffic) -> full cutover.

Attachments: MP_capacity_estimates_Q4.xlsx (breakdown)

Next steps: Rishi — can you sanity-check procurement lead times for H100 reservations and add a pack of fallback variants (quantized A100 options) to reduce cost risk? I will draft the commercial bullet points for procurement.

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren — checked with Supply & Capacity planning: current H100 allocation lead time for reserved pools is ~6-8 weeks for new commitments in US and EU; APAC is ~10-12 weeks due to sourcing cadence. Ops recommends:

- Submit PO + signed SOW by Nov 21 to hit Jan 15 launch if we do parallel procurement and expedite bookkeeping.
- Offer a hybrid commit to reduce sticker shock: commit to H100 for US baseline, propose quantized A100 pool in EU with cross-region compatibility during the pilot (keeps EU-residency requirement by pinning primary nodes in EU).
- Include an explicit fallback policy (hosted fallback with rate-limited traffic) in the first 90 days in case procurement/backfill slips.

Cost mitigation ideas:
- 12-month term vs 24-month term: 12-month gives quicker onboarding but higher monthly than a 24-month which could lower by ~10-15%.
- Auto-eviction policy for burst on-demand nodes to limit cost during extended peaks.

I attached the capacity workbook Lauren prepared and added procurement lead-time notes.
